findings.evidence: Traffic — the request rate the system must sustain, expressed in requests per second (rps) or queries per second, plus concurrency levels and burstiness.
findings.issue: Three-way definitional contradiction about whether concurrency is a workload input. Ch 4 §4.1.1 p.57 lists 'concurrency levels' under the Traffic (workload) dimension; the Preface p.13 operational checklist also lists 'concurrency' under 'What is the workload?'; but Ch 6 §6.1.1 p.111 states flatly 'Concurrency is not a workload input: it is a serving-side quantity derived from the arrival rate and the time in system (Little's law), so it belongs with queue depth on the scheduler side, not in this layer.' Fig 6.1 p.113 then labels the workload box 'rps · token profile · concurrency', and the caption tries to reinterpret the entry as λ.
findings.fix_instruction: Pick one classification and apply it everywhere. Recommended: treat concurrency as a derived serving-side quantity (Ch 6's position), and rewrite Ch 4 §4.1.1 and the Preface p.13 checklist to say 'traffic (rps) and burstiness', moving concurrency out of the workload dimension. Then remove the 'concurrency' entry from Fig 6.1's workload box (or relabel it 'request rate λ').

findings.evidence: The canonical workload is prefill-FLOP- and KV-capacity-dominated, but decode-latency-dominated because of that long context, not because of the ratio — three distinct senses of 'dominated' (share of FLOPs, capacity pressure, share of wall-clock), and the third does not contradict the first two
findings.issue: Prose clarity / semantic overload: the sentence uses 'dominated' three times in one sentence with three different meanings (share of FLOPs, capacity pressure, share of wall-clock) and then apologizes for the overload in a parenthetical rather than fixing the wording. A reader skimming this can misread the canonical workload as decode-bound in the resource sense.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace the overloaded word with three distinct verbs, e.g.: 'The canonical workload's FLOP share is prefill-heavy and its capacity pressure is KV-heavy, but its per-request wall-clock is decode-heavy because of the long output, not because of the input/output ratio — the three are different senses of load and none contradicts the others.'

findings.evidence: Latency TTFT budget 1.2 s (retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s); TPOT budget ~25 ms/token; p95 TTFT ≤ 2 s, p95 TPOT ≤ 35 ms [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] author-chosen user-experience SLO targets; the retrieval-latency contribution (vector DB, same-region) is an assumed estimate (see derivation note beneath the table)
findings.issue: Row-level provenance is incomplete relative to Table 4-2. Table 4-2 (p.75) tags the prefill compute budget 1.08 s as [canonical scenario][DERIVED] (derived as TTFT − retrieval), while Table 4-1 p.58 tags the same latency row (which contains the 1.08 s figure) as [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]. The two tables therefore disagree on the epistemic status of the same derived quantity, and Table 4-1's row-level label does not carry the [DERIVED] half of the split that Table 4-2 applies.
findings.fix_instruction: Split Table 4-1's latency row into two sub-rows or annotate the 1.08 s value inline: 'TTFT budget 1.2 s [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]; prefill budget 1.08 s = TTFT − retrieval [canonical scenario][DERIVED]', matching Table 4-2's row-level split. Alternatively, add an inline note on the 1.08 s value in Table 4-1 pointing to the [DERIVED] tag in Table 4-2.

findings.evidence: Self-host row cell: "capex amortized: 21 × ($350K ÷ 60 mo = $5,833.33 capex + $1,110.33 energy) = $145,816.93, + $10,000 fixed staff (Ch 16)"
findings.issue: Arithmetic inconsistency inside the displayed formula: 21 × ($5,833.33 + $1,110.33) = 21 × $6,943.66 = $145,816.86, but the cell prints $145,816.93 — a $0.07 mismatch between the visible operands and the stated product.
findings.fix_instruction: Recompute the product to $145,816.86 (or restate the per-host operands to more decimal places so the product equals $145,816.93), then verify the subsequent +$10,000 staff line and the $155,816.93 total still reconcile.

findings.evidence: Self-host row cell parenthetical: "capex amortized: 21 × ($350K ÷ 60 mo = $5,833.33 capex + $1,110.33 energy) = $145,816.93"
findings.issue: Component-label mismatch: the cell labels $1,110.33 as "energy" only, but $1,110.33 ÷ 730 hr ≈ $1.52/hr/host is the energy-plus-staff component (the $10,000 staff appears only in the subsequent '+ $10,000' line). The word "energy" understates what the operand contains, or the operand is wrong; either way the label and the arithmetic do not agree.
findings.fix_instruction: Either relabel the $1,110.33 operand (e.g. "energy+misc") or break it into its true energy sub-component so that label, operand, and the separate $10,000 staff line are mutually consistent.

findings.evidence: Ch. 4 sidebar table row: "Self-host — 21-host peak KV-screen fleet ... $155,816.93 ... 21 × ($350K ÷ 60 mo = $5,833.33 capex + $1,110.33 energy) = $145,816.93, + $10,000 fixed staff (Ch 16)"
findings.issue: Arithmetic does not close. $350K ÷ 60 = $5,833.333... per host; × 21 = $122,500.00, not $5,833.33 × 21 as implied. The printed intermediate $145,816.93 = 21 × $6,943.66 (i.e. $5,833.33 + $1,110.33 = $6,943.66 per host; ×21 = $145,816.86). Then $145,816.93 + $10,000 = $155,816.93. So the printed total of $155,816.93 is off by $0.07 from its own derivation, and the energy term $1,110.33 is never derived or sourced in the shown expression.
findings.fix_instruction: Recompute: per-host monthly = $5,833.33 (capex amort) + $1,110.33 (energy) = $6,943.66; × 21 = $145,816.86; + $10,000 staff = $155,816.86. Print $155,816.86 and $145,816.86, and add the derivation of the $1,110.33 energy figure or mark it [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION].

findings.evidence: Table 4-2 rows: "Prefill compute budget — two-term-only upper cap, NOT a feasible deployed prefill target | 1.08 s | [canonical scenario][DERIVED] = TTFT budget (1.2 s) − retrieval (120 ms). This is the residual after only the two dominant terms; it leaves zero allowance for admission/queue and tokenization/transfer..."
findings.issue: Provenance mismatch: 1.08 s is labelled [DERIVED] but it is a pure subtraction of two [ASSUMPTION] inputs (1.2 s TTFT budget and 120 ms retrieval). More importantly, the row is titled a "budget" — an author-chosen ceiling — yet carries the DERIVED tag, whereas the book's own rule (Preface, p. xvii) is that an input or parameter assumption is [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] and only an arithmetically computed value is DERIVED. A budget cap is an assumption; the residual is derived. The row conflates the two in one cell.
findings.fix_instruction: Split the row: keep 1.2 s TTFT budget and 120 ms retrieval as separate [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] rows, and label the 1.08 s residual [canonical scenario][DERIVED]. Keep the 'two-term-only upper cap' qualifier on the derived row.

findings.evidence: Table 4-1, Economic constraints row: "at the ~6-host average the whole-fleet spend is ~$120/hour over the ~173.3 active hours/month (8 h × 260 workdays ÷ 12 = 173.3 h/mo; = $20,800/month), giving ~2.76M input and ~90K output tokens per $1 of fleet spend (active-hours basis)"
findings.issue: Rounding/precision inconsistency: 8 × 260 ÷ 12 = 173.333… h/mo, printed as 173.3; $120 × 173.3 = $20,796, but the same cell prints $20,800 (which is $120 × 173.333…). The book elsewhere (p. 92) prints '6 × 173.3 h × $20' and '$20,800/mo' — the same 1-cent-$4 discrepancy propagates, and 173.3 × 120 = 20,796 ≠ 20,800, so a reader re-deriving from the printed 173.3 gets a different monthly figure than the one used downstream ($/1K req = $20,800 ÷ 6,240K = $3.33).
findings.fix_instruction: Use 173.33 h/mo (or state $20,796) consistently, or explicitly round the monthly spend to the nearest hundred with a note that the $3.33/1K figure derives from the unrounded 173.33 h. The same applies to the p. 92 sidebar derivation.

findings.evidence: Sidebar table: "Cloud, 6 hosts — active-hours basis (6 × 173.3 h × $20) | $20,800 | ≈ $3.33 | 173.3 h/mo = 8 h × 260 workdays ÷ 12 | hour-matched end to end..."
findings.issue: Two problems in one cell. (a) Arithmetic: 6 hosts × 173.3 h × $20/hr = $20,796, not $20,800. (b) Stated-basis inconsistency: the row is described as the 'active-hours basis' for a 6-host fleet, but the numerator as printed ($20,800) equals 6 × $20 × 173.3 h — while the 'Numerator hour basis' column for the same 6-host fleet in the first row reads '730 h/mo (paid occupancy)' with $87,600. The two 6-host rows therefore differ only in hours (730 vs 173.3), which is the book's stated hour-basis mismatch, but the ~$14.04 vs ~$3.33 comparison (4.21× = 730 ÷ 173.3) is only valid if the numerator is computed on the same hours it claims.
findings.fix_instruction: Recompute the active-hours numerator as 6 × 173.33 × $20 = $20,800 (or print $20,796 consistently) and add a one-line note that the 4.21× gap is exactly 730 ÷ 173.33, so a reader can reproduce both ratios.

findings.evidence: Table 4-1, Traffic row: "Lexec = λ × Wexec ≈ 86 (~344 at 40 rps)"
findings.issue: Rendering defect: 'Lexec' is an unformatted plain-text rendering of L_exec (L subscript exec) while the same symbol appears elsewhere as 'L = λ × Wexec' (p. 90) and 'Lexec = λ × Wexec, a separate occupancy' (Table 4-2, p. 96). The three renderings of one symbol are inconsistent, and 'Lexec' is ambiguous with the word 'Lexec' rather than 'L_exec'.
findings.fix_instruction: Standardize the symbol as L_exec (or Lₑₓₑ꜀) in Table 4-1, Table 4-2 and §4.3, and state the symbol once in the Preface's reading conventions.

findings.evidence: Ch. 4 §4.8: "A prefill-throughput cross-check from the Chapter 8 model bounds it from below: 50 rps × 9,200 input = 460,000 prefill tokens/s ÷ ~19,800 tokens/s per host... ≈ ~24 hosts (460,000 ÷ 19,800 = 23.23, ceiled to a whole host)."
findings.issue: Rounding/label defect: 23.23 ceiled is 24, which the text states, but the sentence's leading phrase 'bounds it from below' is misleading — a prefill screen of 24 hosts is 2 hosts below the binding KV screen of 26, so it is a weaker lower bound, and the text later says 'the binding figure is the KV-residency/service-time ~26'. The phrase 'bounds it from below' is technically about the fleet size (24 ≤ 26 ≤ 40) but sits immediately after '≈ ~24 hosts' with a doubled approximation marker ('≈ ~'), a typographic duplication that recurs in the chapter (e.g. '~21 hosts (⌈344/17⌉ = 21)' is fine, but '26 (full util) / ~38 ... 39 before the spare' mixes bare and tilde forms for the same quantity).
findings.fix_instruction: Remove the doubled '≈ ~' and harmonize the approximation markers for the same derived quantity within the paragraph and mini-case; restate the cross-check as 'a weaker lower bound (24 hosts) than the binding KV screen (26 hosts)'.

findings.evidence: "an 80 GB rank runs 99.97% full at 17.5 slots (Ch 7 §7.3 technical note)" (PDF 113). Ch 7 §7.3's notes (PDF 158–159: the three-gate per-rank discussion and "17.5 + 41.94 + 8 = 67.4 GB") never print the 99.97% figure (it is re-derivable as (17.5 + 17.5×3.11296 + 8)/80).
findings.issue: Cross-reference resolves to §7.3, but the cited figure does not appear at the target in §7.3's notes; the pointer is inaccurate even though the number itself is arithmetically correct.
findings.fix_instruction: Add the 99.97%-at-17.5-slots per-rank computation to §7.3's technical note, or soften the Ch 4 pointer to 'derivable from §7.3's per-rank budget'.

findings.evidence: "C = f · N = 0.05 × 2,000 = 100 concurrent users" (PDF 100) vs "C ≈ 17.5 (= 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB, the 9.5K-token resident basis of §4.6) is the analytical quotient, floored to 17 deployable whole-context slots" (PDF 116).
findings.issue: Within the same chapter the symbol C denotes both the active-user population (100) and the per-host KV slot capacity (17.5) — exactly the two quantities the chapter's own argument (population ≠ occupancy ≠ capacity) insists must never be collapsed.
findings.fix_instruction: Rename one use (e.g. U for active users, C reserved for per-host slot capacity) or qualify C at each occurrence.
